changes.name: The Devor Ascendancy
changes.entry:
Type: Nation / Imperial Hive-State
People: Thrx
Common Name: Devor
Government: Collective Hive Intelligence
Foreign Representative: The Emperor

The Devor Ascendancy is one of the great powers of the 99 War.

Foreign maps depict Devor as a nation. Its diplomats speak of borders, treaties, ministries, sovereign rights, and an Emperor. None of these concepts describe it particularly well.

Devor is a hive.

The Thrx recognize no meaningful division between their civilization and their species. Across thousands of miles, millions of Thrx participate in a single enormous collective intelligence. The connection is neither perfect nor instantaneous. Nearby Thrx communicate through pheromones, clicking, posture, and a limited form of telepathy. Across great distances, thought becomes increasingly indistinct.

A precise instruction may become an inclination.

Then an emotion.

Then simply:

Danger.

Pain.

Hot.

Fight.

Specialized Messenger castes race between settlements carrying fresh pheromonal information, allowing distant portions of the hive to synchronize. Consequently, information can take time to cross Devor territory, but eventually the colony knows.

There is only one Emperor.

He does not rule.

The Emperor exists because the Thrx discovered that other peoples expect civilizations to have rulers.

He is an enormous ceremonial organism, roughly twice the height of a human, deliberately bred to appear magnificent and terrifying. His body is adorned in elaborate foreign fashions, his voice has been engineered to reproduce human speech through an unmistakable accompaniment of clicks, and one arm bears an immense vestigial claw designed primarily to make ambassadors reconsider defiance.

The Emperor receives emissaries, signs treaties, issues proclamations, threatens monarchs, and appears to command armies.

He is, in reality, an interface.

When an Emperor dies, the hive can produce another from a selected Crown Larva, altered through the administration of royal jelly.

Brood Queens perform the true reproductive work of Devor. They are not monarchs or personalities of political importance. They are immense biological engines maintained throughout the hive. The collective determines what bodies are required—more workers, more soldiers, more messengers—and the Brood Queens produce them.

Devor cities are almost entirely alien.

Gloss-black towers rise like clustered shells. Bridges resemble articulated limbs. Furnaces pulse beneath buildings. Railways carry great black locomotives whose mechanisms suggest insect anatomy without quite imitating it. Industrial chambers are grown, cast, secreted, bolted, and assembled in methods foreign engineers have difficulty distinguishing from one another.

The elegant coats, lace, medals, hats, ceremonial staffs, and courtly manners associated with the Thrx are largely a deception.

Only those organisms required to communicate with foreign civilizations adopt such things.

Inside Devor, there is nobody to impress.

There is only the work.

Related

The Thrx · The Devor War

posts.name: Gamemaster Only
posts.entry:
The Emperor is not sovereign. He is a deliberately engineered foreign-language interface for the hive. The court, titles, regalia, and apparent hierarchy surrounding him are staged because other nations understand power through individuals.

Orders attributed to the Emperor may have originated elsewhere or emerged through hive consensus. Assassinating him would cause diplomatic confusion and a temporary loss of interface, but it would not decapitate Devor.

The Thrx deliberately encourage foreign intelligence services to overestimate the Emperor’s strategic importance.

changes.name: Thrx
changes.entry:
Type: Humanoid / Insectile Species
Homeland: The Devor Ascendancy
Social Structure: Biologically Engineered Castes

The Thrx are an insectile people whose civilization functions as a single distributed organism.

An individual Thrx is alive, intelligent, and capable of independent action, but individuality is not the normal foundation of Thrx existence.

A Thrx understands itself primarily through purpose.

Worker.

Warrior.

Messenger.

Diplomat.

Furnace-Priest.

Brood Queen.

Emperor.

These are not professions.

They are bodies.

Thrx caste is determined before maturity. Brood Queens alter developing offspring according to the needs communicated by the greater hive. If a district lacks laborers, laborers are produced. If an army has suffered catastrophic losses, new Warrior broods are begun. If diplomatic expansion requires additional representatives capable of foreign speech, Diplomats are engineered.

No caste is inherently more honorable than another.

A Diplomat wearing embroidered velvet before a foreign court is no more important to the hive than the Worker maintaining a drainage conduit beneath the street. Both are organs performing necessary functions.

Communication

Among themselves, Thrx rarely require spoken language.

They communicate through clicking sounds, pheromonal signals, bodily posture, and short-range telepathic impressions.

The telepathic connection weakens considerably with distance. Close members of the hive may exchange surprisingly complex impressions. Across miles, only basic concepts may remain.

Fear.

Food.

Enemy.

Come.

Burning.

Run.

Messenger castes compensate for this limitation by physically carrying pheromonal information through the territory.

Diplomats and the Emperor possess specially developed vocal structures allowing them to imitate the languages of other peoples. Their speech is precise but strange, interrupted by clicks and accompanied by movements and scents whose meanings foreigners generally cannot perceive.

Isolation

A Thrx can survive apart from the hive.

It does not necessarily survive well.

Prolonged isolation commonly produces anxiety, obsessive behavior, confusion, physical illness, and increasingly pronounced individuality.

A severed Thrx may eventually develop personal desires and habits that would scarcely occur within the collective.

Some never recover.

Some cannot bear reconnection.

Major Castes

Brood Queens are enormous reproductive organisms that manufacture the bodies required by the hive.

Workers perform the countless physical and industrial functions upon which Devor depends.

Warriors include enormous beetle-bodied infantry bred for extraordinary strength and durability. Many carry brutal oversized hand-cannons that a human soldier could barely lift.

Messengers are extraordinarily swift organisms responsible for carrying fresh pheromonal instructions across distances where hive communication becomes unreliable.

Furnace-Priests maintain the biological and occult processes through which living energy and souls are extracted, stored, and consumed.

Diplomats are engineered for abstraction, foreign language, negotiation, deception, and cultural mimicry. Their apparent aristocracy is theatrical.

The Emperor is the ultimate expression of that theater: an enormous, regal proxy through which the hive speaks to civilizations that cannot comprehend speaking to a colony.

Related

The Devor Ascendancy · The Devor War

posts.name: Gamemaster Only
posts.entry:
Long-term separation from the hive can produce something the Thrx regard as a serious pathology: a distinct individual.

Severed Thrx may develop private loyalties, irrational preferences, compulsions, personal ambition, and resistance to reintegration. Outsiders may interpret this as the emergence of personhood; the hive interprets it as dysfunction.

Reconnection is not always a cure. A sufficiently changed Thrx may experience the returning hive as an unbearable invasion.

changes.name: The Devor War
changes.entry:
The Thrx do not believe that every form of life possesses equal value.

They regard themselves as the highest form of life.

Everything beneath them is a resource.

This distinction is fundamental to understanding Devor.

The Thrx do not wage war because they hate other peoples.

They do not particularly require hatred.

A forest contains energy.

Animals contain more concentrated energy.

Intelligent creatures contain vastly greater value because intelligence—and particularly the presence of a soul—produces extraordinary yields within Devor extraction systems.

A living captive is more valuable than a corpse.

Consequently, Devor conquest rarely ends in simple extermination.

It ends in agriculture.

Conquered populations are classified, processed, and transferred into enormous agricultural complexes where intelligent beings are maintained as livestock.

Individual captives are frequently sealed inside organic pod-oubliettes: living chambers that restrain the body, regulate nutrition, remove waste, and preserve the inhabitant for future extraction.

Entire conquered populations may disappear into these facilities.

The Thrx consider this perfectly rational.

Their soul furnaces consume the vitality of living creatures to power industry, transportation, cities, weapons, and the machinery of war. Intelligent beings are particularly prized. A single human soul may possess an energy value enormously greater than that of ordinary livestock.

Thrx territory therefore expands for the same reason another nation might seek coalfields, farmland, ports, or iron mines.

Resources.

Before an invasion, Devor surveyors assess a territory not merely for strategic value but for yield.

Forests.

Wildlife.

Livestock.

Population.

Intelligence.

Reproductive capacity.

Soul density.

A successful campaign does not merely capture a province.

It converts an ecosystem into usable inventory.

The 99 War therefore presents the Thrx with an extraordinary opportunity.

Every battlefield creates captives.

Every collapsing nation creates livestock.

Every conquered population can sustain further conquest.

The ultimate Devor war aim is not the destruction of the other great powers.

It is their subjugation.

The Thrx have diplomats because surrender is cheaper than invasion.

They have an Emperor because foreign monarchs prefer surrendering to another monarch.

They sign treaties because treaties can deliver populations without artillery.

They imitate ceremony because ceremony opens gates.

But every negotiation ultimately serves the same objective:

Bring the lesser species beneath Devor control.

Preserve what is useful.

Breed what can be replenished.

Consume what the hive requires.

And continue.

Related

The Devor Ascendancy · The Thrx

posts.name: Gamemaster Only
posts.entry:
Devor field engineers use crude soul-yield equivalences when planning conquest. A healthy human is often valued at roughly twenty horses.

Living, intelligent stock produces far greater and more useful yields than ordinary biomass. This is why Devor prefers capture, preservation, and breeding over battlefield slaughter whenever practical.

Devor peace terms may conceal population quotas, reproductive rights, or tribute measured in living sentient beings rather than money. A treaty that looks surprisingly merciful may simply be a more efficient form of livestock acquisition.
